chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The stipulation (of return) regarding animals is three days for the buyer, whether it was stipulated or not. So if the buyer does something new regarding what he bought before the three days, that is acceptance from him, so there is no stipulation. It was said to him, 'And what is the new occurrence?' He said: 'If he touches, or kisses, or looks at it in a way that was prohibited to him before the purchase.'
ai.seo_question: What is the default period for returning purchased animals in Shia jurisprudence, and what actions void this right?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the 'stipulation of return' (khiyar al-shart) for animal sales, establishing a three-day inspection period where the buyer retains the right to return the goods. It introduces a nuanced Shia legal principle: specific acts of acceptance—such as touching, kissing, or gazing at parts previously forbidden to the buyer—constitute implicit ratification, thereby voiding the stipulation and finalizing the transaction. This reflects the Imami emphasis on the buyer's intent and physical interaction as indicators of consent in commercial jurisprudence.
